selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the place called the atmosphere tell the traveler to do?
questions.answer: It tells him to pay attention to it so he can find the One he is looking for.

questions.question: What is the traveler searching for through his reflections?
questions.answer: He is searching for the One who created him and sent him into the world.

questions.question: How do the clouds serve the earth?
questions.answer: They send water, support life, and help keep conditions suitable.

questions.question: About how fast do the clouds come together when they are commanded to pour rain?
questions.answer: They come together within a very short time, even just a few minutes.

questions.question: What does the quick gathering of clouds suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that they are controlled immediately and exactly.

questions.question: What does the traveler understand about the air from its many duties?
questions.answer: He understands that it is directed with wisdom and generosity.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice about lightning and thunder?
questions.answer: He sees that they also have amazing duties.

questions.question: Why are the raindrops not described as ordinary water only?
questions.answer: Because they are presented as carrying many blessings and acts of kindness.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice after looking at rain?
questions.answer: He then pays attention to lightning and thunder and sees they also have amazing jobs.

questions.question: Who is the guest in the world in this passage?
questions.answer: The traveler is the guest.

questions.question: How is the atmosphere described in a way that mixes strength and kindness?
questions.answer: It seems stern in appearance but gentle in benefit.

questions.question: Besides watering the earth, what else do the clouds help control?
questions.answer: They help adjust the heat needed for life.

questions.question: What does the passage say clouds give to the people and creatures of the earth?
questions.answer: They provide the water needed for life.

questions.question: What comparison helps us imagine the clouds’ obedience?
questions.answer: They are like a trained army following commands.

questions.question: What are some gifts the air brings to living things?
questions.answer: It brings breath, warmth, light, electricity, and sound.

questions.question: Name two things the air carries or transmits.
questions.answer: It transmits sound and carries heat.

questions.question: How are the raindrops described to show beauty?
questions.answer: They are shown as delicate, shining, and sweet.

questions.question: What final understanding does the traveler gain from clouds, wind, rain, and lightning together?
questions.answer: He gains the understanding that all of them are signs working under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What part of creation begins speaking to the traveler in this passage?
questions.answer: The atmosphere, or the open space around the earth, begins speaking to him.

questions.question: What sound in the atmosphere makes the traveler listen carefully?
questions.answer: The strong sound of thunder makes him listen.

questions.question: How do the clouds show order and discipline?
questions.answer: They appear and disappear like a trained army and gather quickly when it is time to send rain.

questions.question: How do clouds show both size and obedience at the same time?
questions.answer: Even though they are huge and can cover the sky, they still disappear and return according to command.

questions.question: What does this quick movement of clouds help prove?
questions.answer: It helps show that they are under control, not acting by themselves.

questions.question: Why is rain linked with mercy in the passage?
questions.answer: Because each drop is described as bringing many caring gifts and helpful jobs from Allah’s mercy.
